label: Corner mast, printed · 45°

tilt_index.hinge: M3 × 60 through both cheeks (54.2 mm of stack)
tilt_index.pin: M3 × 8 into a BLIND 3.0 mm seat

params.shipped_detent_note: 45° is one of the 7 holes on the index fan the head was printed with (40..70° in 5° steps). It is shipped because the DF200 is 87.3° H, not the 60° the pose sweep assumed, so the frame is half as wide again. Moving the pin is not a reprint: only head.stl and retainer.stl turn about the hinge, and spar_lower.stl, spar_upper.stl and every print/*.stl are untouched.

camera_module.note: The DF200 module and its retainer are part of the SET. `df200.stl` is the volumetric stand-in (36 × 36 × 11 body, Ø20 × 9 barrel, Ø13 × 3 hood, 9 × 5 × 4 connector, sensor 4 mm behind the front face), seated in the pocket with its front face on the 3 mm lip. The connector is on the image-UP axis, so it passes the retainer's 24 × 14 window. The retainer boss presses the module's back face by 0.4 mm - the clamp preload; use a 0.5 mm pocket shim behind a thinner module. Measured on the exported meshes: module ∩ head 0.001 mm³, connector ∩ retainer 0.000 mm³.

driver_relief.deck_bolts: Ø7.5 × 26 mm bored up from the plate face at every deck bolt
driver_relief.tool_note: the M3 heads sit in Ø6.6 × 3.2 counterbores, so the tool that enters is a 2.5 mm hex key, not a Ø7 socket. The Ø7 figures are measured from the pad's top face, which is what decides whether a tool can get there.

cable_route.path: retainer 24 × 14 window -> the head's vertical duct -> the hollow spar_upper -> the hollow spar_lower -> the +X cable slot at Z 85..101
cable_route.note: Thread it UP the spar from the +X cable slot BEFORE the Z 285 spigot closes the route, and leave a 60 mm service loop at the head.

bom.deck_inserts: 4x M3 brass heat-set insert (M3 × 5.7, Ø4.6 knurl) melted into the deck grid holes at [(-60.0, -60.0), (-60.0, -40.0), (-60.0, -20.0), (-80.0, -20.0)]. The stock grid hole measures Ø3.50 on the deck plate: open it to Ø4.0 with a hand drill first. The deck plate is 7.0 mm thick (Z 50..57), so a 5.7 mm insert sits flush in it with 1.3 mm to spare.
bom.deck: 4x M3 × 8 socket cap. Head bears at Z 59.80 on a 2.80 mm pad, so 5.20 mm of the 5.70 mm insert is engaged and NOTHING protrudes below the deck - which is what matters, because three of the four bolts sit over the LiPo (pack top Z 46.50, deck underside Z 50.00). No nut, no blind fitting, and the battery stays in.
bom.spigot: 3x M3 × 8, the Z 285 spar spigot: 2 on +X (Z 292 and 301) and 1 on -Y (Z 296.5), each a Ø3.5 clearance hole in the upper half into a Ø2.5 thread-forming pilot in the lower. No pinch clamp and no nuts - the joint is a chamfered rectangle that carries the torque and fixes the pan itself.
bom.hinge: 1x M3 × 60 + nyloc, the head hinge (54.20 mm of stack, 5.80 mm proud)
bom.index: 1x M3 × 8, the tilt index pin. 5.00 mm of cheek + 0.40 mm of gap leaves 2.60 mm in a 3.00 mm BLIND seat, so it cannot reach the camera module (0.00 mm³, measured). An M3 × 12 in the rev-1 through-seat stood 2.9 mm inside the module.
bom.retainer: 2x M3 × 12 self-tapping, the camera retainer (4.00 mm of plate into a Ø2.60 × 9.50 pilot: 8.0 mm of bite)
bom.retainer_plate: PRINT the shared "Camera retainer plate" upgrade - it is this set's retainer, the same solid to 0.005 mm. This set ships no second copy.
bom.shims: PRINT the shared "Camera pocket shims" upgrade if the module is under 11 mm deep: 36 × 36 mm spacers 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 mm thick with the same 24 × 14 window, stackable to 2.8 mm in 0.4 mm steps.

gusset.note: two fins on the deck plate, running out from the spar foot: +Y 5.75 mm, -Y 6.50 mm. There is no collar - the spar's own foot is the gusset, and the deck bolts' Ø7.5 driver reliefs take the room the other two ways.

params.gates_note: Gates: at least 90 % of the tip poses in frame, at most 20 % of the frame on the robot, at least 70 % of the floor, the table visible, and at least 0.8 m of context ahead. Every detent from 40 to 65° passes; 70° fails the context gate at 0.74 m. 45° is shipped because it puts the least of the robot in frame (4.6 % against 8.6 % at 55°), starts the ground at the front wheels (Y 69 mm) and still carries 3.2 m of context.

framing_gates.note: the gripper tip in frame over the floor and table pose sets, the robot itself out of most of the frame, the reachable floor in frame, the table visible, and at least 0.8 m of ground ahead of the near edge

params.framing_source: a 384-pose sweep at the real hFOV 87.3°, run at every detent with the shipped meshes in the scene; the table is printed in DESIGN.md

access_audit.method: Ø7 × 60 driver cast (and Ø3.6 × 60 straight key, and a Ø3.6 cone to 25° for a ball-end key) from each bearing face, against the assembled robot at the parked pose with this mast and the DF200 arch fitted; mm of clear tube
access_audit.verdict: no fastener of this set is blocked and none needs a ball-end key; the deck bolt at (-60, -40) takes 26 mm of Ø7 where the spar's own corner overhangs it, which is what its Ø7.5 × 26 driver relief is for
access_audit.sequence: deck base -> camera cable up the spar -> upper spar on the Z 285 spigot -> 3 spigot screws -> head on the hinge -> index pin -> module -> retainer

shared_plates.retainer: The shared "Camera retainer plate" print-only upgrade - the same solid as this set's own retainer mesh to 0.005 mm (measured on the exported meshes). Printed once, it serves every camera head this project builds: the corner mast and the wrist arch.
shared_plates.pocket_shims: The shared "Camera pocket shims" print-only upgrade - 36 × 36 mm at 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 mm, with the same 24 × 14 window. Stack them for 0.4 to 2.8 mm in 0.4 mm steps.

params.pan: FIXED at the design 10° by the Z 285 spigot section, which is a chamfered rectangle and goes together two ways round only. There is no pan ring and no screw that could give one. To change it, regenerate the spar with a different `pan_deg`.

top.source: user-confirmed JR DF200 "100° without distortion", 640 × 480 MJPG 4:3, rectilinear -> 87.3° H / 71.1° V (2026-09-15)

notes:
Corner mast, printed · 45°. Sensor (-75.3399, -18.5711, 504.8547) at the shipped 45° detent, optical axis (0.122788, 0.696364, -0.707107); hFOV 87.3 / vFOV 71.1 (JR DF200). 3 plates, 249.3 g of PLA, tallest 248.0 mm in Z: `head` 43.4 × 68.5 × 17.5 mm, 17.0 g; `spar_lower` 45.5 × 58.5 × 248.0 mm, 142.3 g; `spar_upper` 58.9 × 60.0 × 229.6 mm, 90.0 g. Robot-frame meshes drawn by the studio: df200.stl, head.stl, retainer.stl, spar_lower.stl, spar_upper.stl.

The plate count is down to the parts that carry load: the list above IS the set. The retainer plate and the pocket shims are the two SHARED print-only upgrades, "Camera retainer plate" and "Camera pocket shims", which this set references instead of shipping a second copy. The retainer is the same solid as this set's own retainer mesh to 0.005 mm, measured on the exported meshes. The tilt index seat in the head is BLIND at 3.0 mm and its pin is M3 × 8, so the pin cannot enter the camera module, and the head's cable duct is vertical and inside the wall.

This is the printed-spar mount, and the default overhead camera mount: three printed plates, no aluminium and nothing drilled. `spar_lower` carries the deck base and the lower spar; `spar_upper` grows the two hinge cheeks and the index fan directly off the top of the tapered spar. There is no metal tube, no base collar, no seat disc, no separate yoke or neck, no pinch clamp and no pan ring. The two halves meet on the Z 285 spigot, a chamfered rectangle that carries the torque AND fixes the pan, so pan is FIXED at the design 10°; regenerate the spar with a different `pan_deg` to change it. The section is symmetric, so a printed witness chevron on the -X face of each half says which way round the joint goes; get it wrong and the camera looks behind the robot. Thread the camera cable up the hollow spar BEFORE the spigot closes. The deck bolts are M3 × 8 into heat-set inserts, so nothing protrudes under the deck and the LiPo stays in. The two spar halves are 248.0 and 229.6 mm tall, so both need 250 mm of Z: an MK4 (220 mm) will not take them, an Ender 3 (250 mm) has 2.0 mm to spare on the taller one.

Hardware beyond the printed plates - the 8 lines of `params.bom`, which the generator builds for THIS variant: `deck_inserts`, `deck`, `spigot`, `hinge`, `index`, `retainer`, `retainer_plate`, `shims`.

Design tilt 55°, shipped detent 45°. The index fan was printed with 7 holes (40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70°) and the head and the retainer are those same meshes rotated about the hinge, so moving the index pin is NOT a reprint and every `print/*.stl` is unchanged by it - `params.shipped_detent_note` records why the shipped hole moved. `df200.stl` is the camera-module stand-in (36 × 36 × 11 body, Ø20 × 9 barrel, Ø13 × 3 hood, 9 × 5 × 4 connector, sensor 4 mm behind the front face) seated in the head pocket at that detent with its front face on the 3 mm lip, connector along the image-UP axis so it passes the retainer's 24 × 14 window. Measured on the meshes this run exported: module ∩ head 0.001 mm³, module ∩ retainer 205.997 mm³, connector ∩ retainer 0.000 mm³.

Assembly order, the fastener-by-fastener driver-access cast and the cable routes are in `ASSEMBLY.md` beside this file; `DESIGN.md` is the design record and the alternatives this one was chosen against. Every measured number behind them is in this set's own `params` block.
summary: THE overhead mount: an over-the-shoulder spar on the rear-LEFT corner, all-PLA and tapered, split at Z 285, whose upper half grows the hinge cheeks and the index fan itself. No metal, no hardware store, THREE plates. The tallest is 248.0 mm, so it needs 250 mm of Z. Sensor (-75.34, -18.57, 504.85) robot mm, 45° nose-down, panned 10°, hFOV 87.3 / vFOV 71.1 (JR DF200). Tilt is a hinge detent, 40..70° in 5° steps; the shipped pin is in the 45° hole.

hinge.positive: a right-hand turn about the axis raises the tilt
